neighbours.label: an opening '{' in Python that is not a plain dict assignment: a {name} placeholder inside a string, a dict passed to % or to a logging call, or a set literal after 'in'
fire: text = "%(user)s logged in at %(time)s" % {'user': u, 'time': t}

notes: Card: all top examples peak on an opening-brace token (' {', '{', " {'", ' {\n'). Probes: '-p {port}' in a string 0.75, 'in {0, 4}' 0.53, '% {'name': …}' 0.40, logging dict 0.31, 'in {1, 15, 30}' 0.24; but 'config = {'host': …}' 0.08, 'data = {}' 0.01, 'return {' 0.14, JavaScript 'function start() {' 0.09, '{}'.format 0.13. Near misses are the same lines with the braces replaced by brackets, parentheses or literals.
